title: Scholastica's storm
hookLine: Benedict's sister prays for rain so he'll stay and talk, and a storm keeps him
last: LISTEN, WITH THE EAR OF THE HEART.

lines: ONE DAY A YEAR, TALKING ABOUT GOD.
cards: Supper is finished. The candles are low. A brother and a sister sit across a table in a small house near his monastery, and they have talked all day about God.

In the story, this is their custom: she comes to see him once a year, and they spend the whole day in praise and holy conversation. Now it's dark. She asks him to stay the night and keep talking until morning.
He says no. He's the man who wrote the rule, and he says he cannot spend the night outside his monastery. So the sister folds her hands on the table, rests her head on them, and prays.

teach.b: The sister is Scholastica, and the story comes from Pope Gregory the Great, who wrote down the life of her brother Benedict.

When Scholastica lifts her head, Gregory says, the thunder breaks, the lightning flashes, and the rain comes down so hard that Benedict and the brothers with him can't put a foot out the door. Benedict is upset.
In Gregory's telling he says, more or less, God forgive you, sister, what have you done? And she answers: I asked you, and you wouldn't listen.

teach.h: I ASKED MY GOD, AND HE LISTENED.
teach.b: So I asked my God, and he listened. Now go, if you can. He can't.
So they stay up all night, and the story says they filled each other with holy conversation until dawn. Why did her prayer win? He was the holier man, wasn't he?
He quotes the letter of John: "God is love."

teach.h: SHE COULD DO MORE: SHE LOVED MORE.
teach.b: Then comes the line that gives today's carry: she could do more, because she loved more. Notice what the story doesn't do. It doesn't say Benedict's rule was wrong.
It says that on one night, love outweighed it. Gregory adds a quiet ending. Three days later, Benedict, standing in his cell, sees his sister's soul rise toward heaven like a dove.
He has her buried in the tomb he had made ready for himself. That was the last time they talked.

how: Christians who keep the old calendar of saints remember Saint Scholastica as Benedict's sister, and Benedictine communities keep her feast and retell the story of the storm.

o: a flood sent to punish a nun who broke the rule
a storm that wrecked Benedict's first monastery
the night a sister's prayer kept her brother talking

games.q: who did what — tap the pairs.
p: prayed with her head on her hands
what Benedict saw three days later

s: in the story, Benedict is the one who gets his way
the storm keeps him at the table all night. his sister's prayer is answered, not his rule.
Gregory says her prayer won because she loved more
he quotes "God is love" and says she could do more because she loved more.
the story says Benedict's rule was wrong
it never says so. it says that on one night, love outweighed the rule.

games.q: you're Benedict. you wrote the rule, and you won't spend a night outside your monastery. your sister, who visits once a year, asks you to stay and talk all night. what do you do?
o: stay. it's one night, and she's your sister.
say no, and get ready to go back.
send the brothers back and stay alone.
games.why: he says no. then she prays, the storm comes, and he can't leave. "I asked you, and you wouldn't listen. I asked my God, and he listened."

practice: Think of one person you usually leave a little early: the call you end first, the visit you cut short because there's a schedule, a rule, a reason.
Picture them across the table, and without fixing anything, notice what you might hear if you stayed ten more minutes. If you pray, name them before God.

wordCard.voice: Scholastica's storm. The night a sister's prayer kept her brother at the table, because, as Gregory tells it, she loved more.

orig.s: illa plus potuit, quae amplius amavit
orig.say: IL-la ploos POH-too-it, kweh am-PLEE-us a-MAH-wit
orig.note: Latin, from Gregory's Dialogues: she could do more, who loved more.

carryVoice: Your line: she loved more. A clear sky, a sudden storm, and a whole night of talk. See you tomorrow.
